title: The Arians' selective quotation and the created/begotten antithesis
english: But the Arians, followers of Arius, say—as they claim—that Christ committed sin. Yet the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19) they neither hold in memory nor utter aloud. Instead, like crafty false accusers and prosecutors, they mutilate the passage and then make their case for the accusation. But lawful contenders must love the truth and embrace all things without omission, not silence one part and tear away another part to present it for deception. For if Christ is created, then he is not begotten; and if he is begotten, he is not created, since both categories cannot apply to the same nature. Everything that has a beginning also admits an end, and everything that admits an end is capable of corruption.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by attacking how the Arians quote Scripture about Christ, then moves to the logical incompatibility of 'created' and 'begotten.'
